summary: Tested user-menu dropdown navigation fix. The dropdown OPENS and is visually rendered, but menu items (My Profile / My Deck / Trades / Edit Profile / Log out) DO NOT navigate when clicked. Outside-click close and toggle-close behaviors work correctly. Root cause is a CSS stacking-context bug — NOT the React 18 setOpen race the fix targeted. The <main> element paints on top of the header dropdown and intercepts pointer events, so clicks land on <main> instead of the menu buttons.

ui_bugs.issue: Dropdown items are unclickable because <main> covers them and intercepts pointer events. Playwright reports '<main> intercepts pointer events' on every menu-* click. elementFromPoint at the center of [data-testid=menu-profile] returns <MAIN>, not the button. Because the click never reaches the button, nav() never fires and the URL stays on /feed. This is exactly the user-reported symptom ('they open nothing') — the previous fix (buttons + useNavigate + outside-click ref) did not address the real cause.

action_items: Fix z-index stacking so the header dropdown renders above <main>. The offending rule is in /app/frontend/src/index.css line 110: `#root > * { position: relative; z-index: 2; }`. Because #root selector has higher specificity than Tailwind's .z-40, the <header sticky top-0 z-40> is FORCED to z-index:2. <main> is also #root>* → z-index:2 + position:relative, creating its own stacking context that (as a later DOM sibling) paints on top of the header. The z-50 on the dropdown is only local to header's stacking context, so it cannot escape above <main>.

Recommended fixes (any one):  (a) Change index.css rule to exclude header, e.g. `#root > main, #root > footer { position: relative; z-index: 1; }` and let header use its own z-40, OR  (b) Override header specifically: `header.sticky { z-index: 40 !important; }`, OR  (c) Render the dropdown in a Portal to document.body with a fixed position anchored to the button (most robust).
After the CSS fix, re-run the same dropdown navigation checks to confirm menu-profile/deck/trades/settings/logout all navigate.
critical_code_review_comments: index.css rule `#root > * { position: relative; z-index: 2; }` silently defeats every Tailwind z-* utility applied to direct root children — landmine for future dropdowns/modals/toasts. Remove or scope narrowly.
Header.jsx z-40 is not effective due to the above; consider portalling overlays out of sticky/scroll containers.
Sticky element (`sticky top-0`) already creates its own stacking context; children with z-50 cannot escape above later-sibling stacking contexts of equal/greater z-index.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug is a CSS stacking issue, not React. Verify by: login as admin, open user menu, then in devtools console run `document.elementFromPoint(...)` on the menu item center — it must return the <button data-testid=menu-*>, not <main>. Then click each item and confirm URL changes to /u/luna_admin, /collection, /trades, /settings, and /login (logout). Landmark testids expected: profile-rarity, 'YOUR COSMIC DECK' text, trades-tab-incoming, settings-username-input, login-submit.
rca of the issue: CSS rule `#root > * { position: relative; z-index: 2; }` in /app/frontend/src/index.css:110 gives <header> and <main> the same z-index:2 with their own stacking contexts. <main> is a later DOM sibling of <header>, so it paints ON TOP of the header. The dropdown's local z-50 (inside header stacking context of z:2) cannot rise above <main>. The dropdown is therefore visually visible (main has transparent bg) but pointer events land on <main>, so button onClick never fires and nav() never runs — exactly matching the user report that the menu items 'open nothing'. Reproduction: login as admin → click luna_admin avatar → click 'My Profile' → URL remains /feed. Playwright confirms with 'main intercepts pointer events' and elementFromPoint returning <MAIN>.
